question: Can a TOST equivalence test or confidence-interval upper bound on |r| formally confirm behavioral-structural signal orthogonality at the existing n=480 paired samples, and what practical equivalence margin (delta) is achievable versus required for C-FRESHNESS product architecture decisions?
hypothesis: The parent EXP-GRAPH-35308806969 established near-zero pooled correlation (|r|=0.0335, r²=0.001) on n=480 paired samples from 8 co-occurring conditions on deterministic Flask 3.1.3 + PyJWT HS256 localhost. The frozen permutation p=0.465 failed the conjunctive C3 gate, but power analysis confirmed n=480 is provably underpowered for |r|=0.05 at permutation p<0.05 (minimum n=1538). This experiment tests whether a TOST equivalence test or CI upper bound can confirm |r|<delta at practical sample sizes, replacing the permutation test. The 95% CI upper bound on r is approximately 0.122 (Fisher z-transform, n=480), which is <0.15 (passes delta=0.15) but NOT <0.10 (fails delta=0.10). TOST at delta=0.15 should pass; TOST at delta=0.10 should fail. The experiment maps the full delta-vs-sample-size trade-off surface.
falsifier: The hypothesis is falsified if: (1) C1_drift_tp fails (mean TP < 0.85 OR any Wilson lower CI < 0.75) — inherited from parent and not retested, only verified against parent metrics; OR (2) C2_variance fails (< 6/8 conditions with std > 0 for both signals) — inherited and verified; OR (3) C3_equivalence fails: NO tested delta (0.10, 0.12, 0.15, 0.20) achieves TOST pass (95% CI upper bound on |r| >= all tested deltas); OR (4) C4_null_control fails (FP > 0.0) — inherited and verified. If C1-C2-C4 PASS and C3 fails for delta=0.10 but passes for delta=0.15, the result is MIXED with bounded ceiling. If C3 fails for ALL deltas, behavioral and structural signals are confirmed non-orthogonally and the architecture pivots to fused classifiers.

baselines.description: Parent EXP-GRAPH-35308806969 at n=480: |r|=0.0335, r²=0.001, permutation p=0.465, C1-C2-C4 PASS, C3 FAIL (underpowered). This experiment reanalyzes the same paired samples with TOST/CI instead of permutation test.
baselines.expected: 95% CI upper bound on |r| approximately 0.122, confirming underpowering diagnosis

baselines.description: 95% CI for r via Fisher z-transform: z ± 1.96/√(n-3), back-transformed. At n=480, SE=0.04585, CI approximately (-0.056, 0.122).
baselines.expected: Upper bound ~0.122, achieving delta=0.15 but not delta=0.10

baselines.description: TOST at delta ∈ {0.10, 0.12, 0.15, 0.20}: two one-sided tests H0: |r| >= delta vs H1: |r| < delta, each at alpha=0.05.
baselines.expected: Pass at delta >= 0.15, fail at delta <= 0.10

positive_control.description: Verify parent established results: TP=1.0, 8/8 conditions with variance, FP=0.0. These are inherited measurements — this experiment does NOT re-run the Flask server. The control verifies data integrity of the parent raw_evidence.
positive_control.expected: All parent metrics replicate from raw_evidence/experiment_data.json

null_control.description: Verify parent null control: FP=0.0 on 240 noise-only samples. Inherited from parent raw_evidence.

measurement_validity: No new HTTP request/response cycles are made — this is a frozen statistical reanalysis of parent EXP-GRAPH-35308806969 raw_evidence/experiment_data.json

Parent data collection: Flask 3.1.3 + PyJWT 2.14.0 HS256 localhost, graded session_status_check (401->1.0, 403->0.5, 500->0.75), session_change=1 for ALL session_invalidation samples, 60 samples per condition, 8 co-occurring conditions, 4 noise-only conditions, SEED=42
Parent measurement validity preserved: all behavioral signals from real HTTP cycles, structural signals from unauthenticated /schema endpoint, drift patterns identical to parent
TOST/CI computation uses standard Fisher z-transform: z = 0.5*ln((1+r)/(1-r)), SE = 1/√(n-3), CI = tanh(z ± z_{α}*SE)
TOST null hypothesis H0: |r| >= delta, alternative H1: |r| < delta. Significance level alpha=0.05 for each one-sided test. Two-sided equivalence requires BOTH one-sided tests to reject.
Equivalence margins chosen to bracket the product-relevant threshold: delta=0.10 (<1% shared variance, strict), delta=0.12 (<1.44%), delta=0.15 (<2.25%, moderate), delta=0.20 (<4%, lenient)
decision_rule: PASS if ALL of: (1) C1_drift_tp verified from parent: mean TP >= 0.85 AND all Wilson lower CI > 0.75; (2) C2_variance verified from parent: >= 6/8 conditions with std > 0 for both signals; (3) C3_equivalence: 95% CI upper bound on |r| < delta for at least one tested delta ∈ {0.10, 0.12, 0.15, 0.20}, reported as TOST-equivalent; (4) C4_null_control verified from parent: FP = 0.0. FAIL if any fails. MIXED if C1-C2-C4 PASS and C3 passes only for delta >= 0.15 (upper bound 0.10-0.15 range untested). The decision rule replaces the parent's permutation p<0.05 with a CI upper bound test, which is the appropriate procedure for very-low-magnitude correlations where the question is 'is |r| small enough?' not 'is |r| exactly zero?'
product_consequence_positive: If CI upper bound < 0.15 (or lower), C-FRESHNESS orthogonality is formally confirmed at that margin. Product pipeline integrates behavioral + structural as independent parallel channels with quantified shared-variance ceiling < 2.25%.
product_consequence_negative: If CI upper bound >= 0.20 for all tested deltas, behavioral and structural signals are not practically independent. Product architecture pivots to fused classifiers. If CI upper bound is 0.10-0.15, the product decision depends on delta tolerance: delta=0.15 acceptable → parallel channels; delta=0.10 required → need n~1538 or accept fused classifiers.
estimated_cost: Minimal: statistical reanalysis only, no new data collection. Compute TOST/CI on existing 480 paired samples from parent raw_evidence.
expected_information_gain: Very High: directly resolves the single remaining frozen gate (C3) for C-FRESHNESS with a decision-relevant equivalence margin. Maps the full delta-vs-sample-size trade-off surface. Changes a product architecture decision (parallel vs fused channels) regardless of outcome.
